title: Apple, Meta reject OKX–ICE tokenized stock plans, leaving crypto firms as the ones to watch
content: Strategy, Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood are among six companies from the venture’s initial selection with no disclosed objection, after 90% of issuers opted out.

title: U.S. prediction markets regulator issues demand that clashes directly with courts
content: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said regulated exchanges can't cut off customers state-by-state, but firms like Kalshi are under court orders to do so.

title: The crypto industry has found new ways to grow. Making money from them is another story
content: Coinbase, Robinhood and Circle are expanding into stablecoins, payments and prediction markets, but their latest earnings show how hard it is to escape crypto's boom-and-bust cycles.

title: Thailand moves to block Bitget as crypto exchange's local acquisition faces uncertainty
content: Thailand’s SEC filed a criminal complaint against Bitget’s operator, alleging it ran an unlicensed crypto exchange for Thai users from 2022 to 2025.

title: U.S. added 165,000 jobs in October, blowing past 65,000 estimate
content: The unemployment rate unexpectedly fell to 4.1%. The strong showing surely puts a December rate hike in play, but next week's inflation numbers and the fate of the stock market could prove more important.

title: Nvidia may face a more hostile post-election Washington: Report
content: CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump probably won’t save the company from a more adversarial Washington, Semafor says.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
content: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions
content: The US Treasury bureau FinCEN on Friday ordered US financial institutions to stop processing transfers involving MEXC Global.

title: Gnosis Pay breach exposes card details, personal data and crypto wallet information
content: The crypto debit card provider said customer funds remained safe despite the exposure of sensitive financial and personal information.

title: Binance hack is ‘cyber war,’ TRM Labs executive says
content: TRM Labs executive Ari Redbord called for governments to take offensive action against North Korean hackers following the record $6.3 billion Binance theft.

title: Treasury Cuts Crypto Exchange MEXC Off From US Financial System
content: FinCEN’s order, part of Operation Economic Outcast, bars U.S. institutions from any transfers to or from MEXC, which Treasury says facilitated $16 billion in illicit finance tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia.

title: Greece Passes Crypto Tax Law With 10% Gains Levy, 15% on Staking and DeFi
content: Greece has approved a crypto tax framework with a €500 ($557) annual gains threshold and new rules for staking and DeFi income, but lawmakers left important questions about token swaps unresolved.

title: Why a Hyperliquid Treasury Firm Wants to Become a US Futures Broker
content: Hyperliquid Strategies has applied to become a U.S. futures commission merchant, a move that could let Americans trade perpetual futures on permissioned Hyperliquid markets, pending regulatory approval.

title: Paraguay Protests Over Bank Lockout Intensify as Impeachment Vote Nears
content: Savers locked out of Ueno Bank burned their cards, booed a former presidential candidate out of the crowd, and watched Congress move to remove President Peña.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $430 Million as Tech Rout Tests Wall Street Buyers
content: Fidelity and BlackRock led Thursday's Bitcoin ETF withdrawals as a technology-stock selloff rattled risk assets.

title: U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
content:
Bitcoin Magazine

U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows
FinCEN issued a final order under section 9714(a) that will bar U.S. financial institutions from sending or receiving funds with MEXC Global 30 days after Federal Register publication, citing at least $16 billion in alleged illicit activity.
